speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; these are significant symptoms I need to investigate carefully. To begin, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms and if there is any recent history of insect bites or exposure to sick animals?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent camping trip in Minnesota and your history of sexually active behavior are significant risk factors. Given the fever, joint pain, and new wrist pain, do you notice that the skin lesions are on your extremities or your trunk, and are there any rashes on your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF). The combination of fever, chills, malaise, a history of camping in Minnesota, and specifically "violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands" with severe wrist swelling is highly characteristic of early RMSF, which often presents with a rash on the extremities and palms before spreading centrally. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide close-up clinical photos of the wrist lesions and the palms/soles to confirm the rash morphology. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with Differential. REQUEST TEST: Indirect Fluorescent Antibody (IFA) test for Rickettsia rickettsii.
